scope: Install post-exec compiler instrumentation before explicitly releasing compiler execution while preserving production process/cgroup ownership and real collected termination outcomes. This source audit does not establish runtime acceptance.

public_gating.claim: Session child gating holds children until explicit resume; sync enable/disable wrappers forward checked requests.

public_device_signals.claim: Device child_added observes gated children; child_removed means resumed OR gone, not a collected exit status.

public_device_resume.claim: Device.resume(pid) forwards to host resume; public C frida_device_resume_sync is process release.

session_resume_is_not_process_release.claim: Session.resume reconnects a persisted/disconnected session; it does not release the execution gate.

linux_execve_monitor.claim: Linux SpawnMonitor attaches to libc execve export, the existing NativeCalls.execve binding target.

exec_metadata.claim: Linux exec on_enter records origin EXEC, pid=current PID and parent_pid=current PID (synthetic self-exec ancestry), copies path/argv/envp then synchronously prepares exec; on_leave cancels a failed exec.

blocking_exec_preparation.claim: Exec calling thread waits for prepare_to_exec completion using native condition variable; no timing-based attach race is required.

agent_child_gating.claim: First child-gating subscriber installs ForkMonitor and SpawnMonitor.

exec_replacement.claim: Old entry marked PROCESS_REPLACED; prepare exec transition; await exec; await old entry closed; add pending child. No assumption that the old session/script survives exec.

pending_resume.claim: Device resume removes pending child, handles pending ack or resume request, otherwise platform resume.

linux_platform_resume.claim: Linux exec prepare/await/cancel delegate to helper; perform_resume delegates to helper resume.

linux_exec_stop.claim: ExecTransitionSession starts tracing, waits TRAP, single steps, waits TRAP. Zero instructions after exec is not the implementation contract.

linux_resume_releases_exec_stop.claim: Helper resume removes/closes ExecTransitionSession to release process; invalid PID produces typed native error.

injector_may_advance_loader.claim: Injector can repeat bootstrap after libc load and resume target until dynamic-linker r_brk when TOO_EARLY. No promise of zero loader/pre-main allocations before instrumentation.

gating_disable_can_resume.claim: Subscriber count zero automatically requests resume for pending children matching parent_pid; do not disable/detach as a fail-closed substitute for owner termination.

child_borrowed_data.claim: Child exposes pid,parent_pid,origin,optional path/argv/envp; from_info creates signal object. Copy data in callback; do not retain borrowed pointer without a native reference.

smallest_candidate.choice: Attach and enable child gating on the existing prepared LinuxProcessTree Java gate, then handle its same-PID EXEC replacement; retain existing LinuxSupervisor and LinuxCgroup owners.
smallest_candidate.why_plain_attach_before_release_insuffic: Gate is a JVM replaced by libc execve. Loading allocator instrumentation into that JVM does not install it in the new compiler image; attaching only after ordinary release races compiler startup.
smallest_candidate.why_frida_spawn_not_selected: frida_device_spawn_sync creates a Frida-owned launch path. Substituting it would change current supervisor parentage, privilege drop, stream handling and status ownership; unnecessary for the existing gate boundary.
sequence: Initialize pinned Frida and dispatcher using already accepted lower-level Java/FFM lifecycle; retain typed GErrors and original failures.

Call production LinuxSupervisor.prepare(...). It creates outer containment, moves dedicated supervisor before permitting helper creation, prepares gate, verifies action-group placement, and returns stable rootPid without workload release.

Connect Device child-added/child-removed signals and gate Session detached signal before releasing workload; callbacks copy identity fields/reason into Java queue and return. Do not block callback dispatcher with synchronous attach/load/resume work.
frida_device_attach_sync(local_device, rootPid, session_options_or_NULL, cancellable, error). Gate remains waiting for production release.
frida_session_enable_child_gating_sync(gate_session,cancellable,error) must return successfully before LinuxSupervisor.release(). No compiler allocator hook in pre-exec JVM is required.

Call existing LinuxSupervisor.release(), which publishes release and waits supervisor acknowledgement. Existing trusted gate drops uid/gid then invokes native libc execve at the SAME rootPid. Release acknowledgement is not compiler-hook readiness.

Join old-session PROCESS_REPLACED detach and matching Device child-added event as states; do not rely on Java callback arrival order. EXEC event must have pid=rootPid, synthetic parent_pid=rootPid, expected compiler path/argv; Linux proc parent remains dedicated supervisor. A fork/spawn event or unrelated device process is not this root replacement.

Keep compiler pending. Attach a NEW native Session to the same rootPid, connect its lifecycle and script message handlers, create/load fresh compiler instrumentation. Require authentic hook-ready token/PID/image identity and hook-resolution success. Old gate Session/Script objects are not reused for the compiler.

If compiler descendants must also be intercepted, enable child gating on NEW compiler Session before resuming it; each descendant image needs its own verified identity and script. Do not treat initial gate subscription as inherited across exec.
Only after compiler hook-ready call frida_device_resume_sync(device,rootPid,cancellable,error). Never substitute frida_session_resume_sync.

Keep supervisor root/adopted reaping and cgroup termination unchanged. Natural completion uses LinuxSupervisor.observeCompletion()/result(); cancellation first requests LinuxSupervisor.terminate(), then retains actual result. Frida detached/child-removed events and cgroup emptiness cannot replace process waits.

After owner proves collection (or retains failed cleanup ownership), unload/detach only live applicable sessions, disconnect handlers, release old/new script/session/device/manager refs, join dispatcher, shutdown/deinit then close callback arena as already accepted. Preserve cleanup errors; do not disable gating before owner termination when intending fail-closed cleanup.

required: Before production release, child-gating enable completed for prepared rootPid.

Fresh compiler session/script emits authentic hook-ready while rootPid is still in Frida pending children and action cgroup; no device.resume was sent yet.
Then explicit device.resume returns and real compiler produces expected artifact/output and actual owner-collected root/adopted statuses.
On cancellation before Frida resume, existing supervisor/cgroup owner can terminate/reap without auto-resume substituting for cleanup.

steps: Use one tiny deterministic real rustc compilation as existing Launch command; call production prepare, record rootPid/PPid/action-group and unchanged source hashes.
Connect copied event queue, attach prepared gate, enable child gating, then production release; capture same-PID EXEC and PROCESS_REPLACED with actual identities.

Without device.resume, attach fresh compiler session/load minimally diagnostic allocator hook and require authentic compiler-image hook-ready; enumerate_pending_children confirms pending PID. Record libc/bootstrap boundary limitations, not a zero-loader-allocation claim.
